Current family 'merge-readiness-without-current-head-review-authority' invariant: The final Merge Readiness controller must itself fail closed unless a complete exact-head review exists at the current PR head and verifies against trusted PR evidence -- a missing, stale, incomplete, or still-contested review is a hard merge blocker, never a warning. The review authority is an ordered reviewer pool declared by the trusted default branch, and that declaration is what names its members: authority-eligible reviewers are attempted in strict priority order, a reviewer the pool marks triage-only (authority_eligible false) is never review authority however substantive its output, and the deterministic hostile-review guard the pool declares as its last_resort is the last resort. Any reviewer below the primary is admissible only when it records, in machine-checkable fields (reviewer_attempts), that every higher-priority authority-eligible reviewer was actually attempted and exhausted with a recorded reason and recorded budgets within the bounded timeout policy -- acknowledgement and review are separately budgeted, so an attempt proves exhaustion only when both recorded budgets are within policy and the review budget was actually spent; the guard is admissible only when the whole enabled pool is exhausted AND it records why the pool reviewers could not review and that Governance, trusted Preflight, a zero unresolved-thread count, and complete structured evidence were all green at review time. A review that silently skips an enabled reviewer while it is available, a guard review whose exhaustion cannot be proven (missing, skipped, duplicated, malformed, unknown-agent, or out-of-bounds attempts), a review whose recorded exact head differs from the candidate head, or a new commit after the review all invalidate the review and force reviewer selection to restart. A resolved review finding counts as satisfied only when its structured evidence names the exact-head correction commit and a regression test committed in the change set. Current family 'lifecycle-event-wiring-asymmetry' invariant: If a downstream gate reacts to a lifecycle transition and requires an upstream trusted artifact or cycle to already exist, that transition must also have a trusted event-driven path that creates or reconciles the prerequisite, and every legitimate state that path can report -- including an in-progress wait, not only success or absence -- must be a state the consumer explicitly recognizes. This binds every lifecycle transition the downstream gate reacts to, and it binds in particular the two classes of transition that can invalidate an existing prerequisite: one that makes review *required* (Draft -> Ready for Review), and one that changes the *exact HEAD* the prerequisite is bound to (synchronize, i.e. a push). A transition of either class must be wired directly on the trusted prerequisite producer; a schedule or an unrelated producer's `workflow_run` completion is a bounded recovery fallback, never the primary mechanism, because a fallback that depends on some other workflow completing first is silent about the case where that workflow never completes. A trigger existing is not sufficient, a workflow step exiting SUCCESS is not proof of materialization, a fallback path is not a primary path, and a classifier that treats any unrecognized-but-legitimate producer state as failure is this same asymmetry wearing a consumer gap instead of a missing trigger.
